output.reasoning:
This posting fails on role type, seniority, and skills fit.

(1) Role type: The title is 'Principal Engineer Capacity/Compute' in the 'Software Engineering - Infrastructure' department. The work is capacity engineering: data pipelines that ingest fleet telemetry into BigQuery, observability tooling (Prometheus/PromQL/Grafana), Kubernetes operations, scheduling and fragmentation fixes, and cost attribution and forecasting across cloud providers. The posting describes it as 'a hands-on engineering role with a devops flavor.' It does not involve building, training, or deploying ML/NLP systems, so it doesn't match her target roles (ML Engineer, AI Engineer, Applied NLP Engineer, Research Engineer). ML systems come up only as the workloads whose hardware utilization gets measured.

(2) Level: 'Principal' is a very senior title. The posting asks for 'a strong track record building and operating production systems' and 'Deep experience with at least one major cloud provider... and its operations,' and the $320,000–$485,000 salary band confirms a principal-level hire. Ananya finishes her BU MS in 2026-12, and her only industry experience is an 8-month ML Engineer co-op (2026-01 to 2026-08). That is not realistic for this level.

(3) Skills fit: The required section names more than two technologies: Python, SQL/BigQuery SQL, a major cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure), Prometheus, PromQL, and Grafana. She has shipped Python, SQL, and AWS, so the numeric overlap test passes. However, the role also requires operating Kubernetes-native systems at scale (collection agents, workload labeling, taint/reservation/scheduling behavior). Kubernetes appears only in her familiar_with_not_shipped list. Under her rules, an un-shipped core requirement like Kubernetes makes the posting NOT_RELEVANT. She also has no observability-stack (Prometheus/Grafana) experience.

(4) Location: New York City, NY, hybrid with at least 25% office time. This is US-based and she is willing to relocate, so it passes.

(5) Sponsorship: The posting says 'We do sponsor visas!' with reasonable-effort caveats, and does not disclaim sponsorship. She needs sponsorship, so this passes.

Location and sponsorship pass, but the role is infrastructure/devops capacity engineering rather than ML engineering, it is principal level, and it depends on un-shipped Kubernetes. Each of these alone excludes it.
